Alcohol metabolism is `the biochemical process by which the body breaks down and eliminates ingested alcohol (ethanol), primarily in the liver` . Most ethanol is converted into harmless byproducts—carbon dioxide and water—while a small percentage leaves the body unchanged in urine, breath, and sweat.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdgHEIkXXIp1BF5tL2rOTW2-LHHbffwhgkh3byH2zDWBF3YKJgFtIz_HVUBeXjwCx3fXbyyHN3ZJZUQdcV6MdGC2fUgJWLkMMjfJD_MbslHOd_GzkyFTZOp00EbAfZuvI7iN6EzmBBVuFBtYdj458TdmqyXUwIso)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbgHEIkXXFLcgtd6RR4ZbE5XIRbIIimYF656jc8sAsigCepxtoLbUtspVYkdgY3ttPUKthJn76FTfsfPZe_NLYIIBlO2qCgVdZOWpJZKpJDtznoC3wpJqPCCOjHcWDJAIHJ_R4E_9rWFxu-VVcVys)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEScgHEIkXXpVflEqKYCEK06oquTD44dZUWRPK4Xvoei-iNnLFcpTyccmG0w9Dgy9ieV_CoSX9nQ3m1uxtGtmfoAyVzKf7S9Phh6S0KfbVSFeEmvhGJxE_ocge7G26Trp86UAiouvyVHoUjZ9YvZhBjTwC0TQ)

### How the Body Breaks Down Alcohol

- **Absorption:** After swallowing, alcohol enters the bloodstream mainly through the small intestine and stomach, then travels to the liver.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbgHEIkXXFLcgtd6RR4ZbE5XIRbIIimYF656jc8sAsigCepxtoLbUtspVYkdgY3ttPUKthJn76FTfsfPZe_NLYIIBlO2qCgVdZOWpJZKpJDtznoC3wpJqPCCOjHcWDJAIHJ_R4E_9rWFxu-VVcVys)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESiAEBxCJF1_mOI6z9U48yGhYeul_NO92Kjzh128A6AMvH6-PtWNTufqSgUqySRcy4BN7lFB4pi1H_IICZu9W27a2bRX-B03bEeKXRoxJi5Dov0oA1pwvIpSjMYsacNuychBqVjPhtTcc8e-uQcgIyUAgghxcbyJJENhrT_-Oi2GygjnmOVLkPes6m)
- **Step 1 (Ethanol to Acetaldehyde):** The enzyme **alcohol dehydrogenase (ADH)** converts ethanol into **acetaldehyde** , a toxic compound and known carcinogen.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdgHEIkXXIp1BF5tL2rOTW2-LHHbffwhgkh3byH2zDWBF3YKJgFtIz_HVUBeXjwCx3fXbyyHN3ZJZUQdcV6MdGC2fUgJWLkMMjfJD_MbslHOd_GzkyFTZOp00EbAfZuvI7iN6EzmBBVuFBtYdj458TdmqyXUwIso)[[2]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ArwZfswz9sc)
- **Step 2 (Acetaldehyde to Acetate):** The enzyme **aldehyde dehydrogenase (ALDH)** —primarily mitochondrial ALDH2—quickly converts acetaldehyde into **acetate** , a less toxic substance.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdgHEIkXXIp1BF5tL2rOTW2-LHHbffwhgkh3byH2zDWBF3YKJgFtIz_HVUBeXjwCx3fXbyyHN3ZJZUQdcV6MdGC2fUgJWLkMMjfJD_MbslHOd_GzkyFTZOp00EbAfZuvI7iN6EzmBBVuFBtYdj458TdmqyXUwIso)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbgHEIkXXFLcgtd6RR4ZbE5XIRbIIimYF656jc8sAsigCepxtoLbUtspVYkdgY3ttPUKthJn76FTfsfPZe_NLYIIBlO2qCgVdZOWpJZKpJDtznoC3wpJqPCCOjHcWDJAIHJ_R4E_9rWFxu-VVcVys)
- **Final Elimination:** Acetate moves out of the liver into other tissues, where it is broken down into carbon dioxide and water. Roughly 90%–98% of ingested ethanol is metabolized, while about 5%–10% is excreted unchanged via breath, urine, and sweat.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEScgHEIkXXpVflEqKYCEK06oquTD44dZUWRPK4Xvoei-iNnLFcpTyccmG0w9Dgy9ieV_CoSX9nQ3m1uxtGtmfoAyVzKf7S9Phh6S0KfbVSFeEmvhGJxE_ocge7G26Trp86UAiouvyVHoUjZ9YvZhBjTwC0TQ)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdgHEIkXXIp1BF5tL2rOTW2-LHHbffwhgkh3byH2zDWBF3YKJgFtIz_HVUBeXjwCx3fXbyyHN3ZJZUQdcV6MdGC2fUgJWLkMMjfJD_MbslHOd_GzkyFTZOp00EbAfZuvI7iN6EzmBBVuFBtYdj458TdmqyXUwIso)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEStgEBxCJF1586n34yf9ax6JJG1zHafunqJ5MVRPeB0tYrtKr6hQqOsEajxhO6D6E6xzkBKF7Cx3VTPbXy9HkN_TDVcIsB06Q1MAD3A6zwNsCSn5SSeuysplbhdjw5MbdIdK4OGEFs5iTR8w4kaW5Dsb0OGjvY2CvBh4fbEqcJem8Zmf1wYfw2otw_0QLUpZo_sSTOWnFFP1cG2KXOQ_sleiuL3gMccrApg2k7C-klh6LhlgyBCh5VtA)

### Secondary Pathways and Rate

- **Alternative Enzymes:** At high alcohol concentrations or with heavy drinking, secondary pathways—such as **CYP2E1** (part of the microsomal ethanol oxidizing system) and **catalase** —also help oxidize ethanol to acetaldehyde.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESeQHEIkXXPyPmgZPwagj1Dd4OWuEMmagOaiWtk1ky76vYeyWfoJnlw3XAgGMnmqhAT6MYip4cP6W4VTYIVUYGQNx0CKb3EsAQvb33Gbhr3AAd4FjfcpDEGNmZTroxBOQncpGFphIIbhYH2p3PN8mcpx7XCWpbz37PvIY)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbgHEIkXXFLcgtd6RR4ZbE5XIRbIIimYF656jc8sAsigCepxtoLbUtspVYkdgY3ttPUKthJn76FTfsfPZe_NLYIIBlO2qCgVdZOWpJZKpJDtznoC3wpJqPCCOjHcWDJAIHJ_R4E_9rWFxu-VVcVys)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEStgEBxCJF1586n34yf9ax6JJG1zHafunqJ5MVRPeB0tYrtKr6hQqOsEajxhO6D6E6xzkBKF7Cx3VTPbXy9HkN_TDVcIsB06Q1MAD3A6zwNsCSn5SSeuysplbhdjw5MbdIdK4OGEFs5iTR8w4kaW5Dsb0OGjvY2CvBh4fbEqcJem8Zmf1wYfw2otw_0QLUpZo_sSTOWnFFP1cG2KXOQ_sleiuL3gMccrApg2k7C-klh6LhlgyBCh5VtA)
- **Fixed Pace:** The liver clears alcohol at a relatively steady rate (often cited as roughly one standard drink per hour, or a blood alcohol concentration drop of about 0.015% per hour). Drinking coffee, taking cold showers, or drinking water does not speed up this metabolic rate.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESlwEBxCJF11VA0JEqCBgXI7AJAn8mz2tqsJuBq81JHPiFsGeT5y55koG9gzZjcRaFcyA06flg8u43NUG7sFe_8MXRwhSofXiVFfXAaFbQ7thZPpgQMjIwbV4ecRFlv1gieMf2-yG8Fchnfdqpec_eu9R9Gj4rUeXZzwZ-LvbzgbMPgNQFlMpaiMKqBUFgQzjiwU5Cs_Ap6IcJ)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESnQEBxCJF16GZbKqjkpS5NWxe5Igs6f0Iu43bSWQXOGD732Vr3Vbcgn-9LjF0hlcb2V-hy7_T__ulsVDS64hFpm6a13obqzZGxdUARIRcyJ8KxwFfB_2FayF9736V4bs-fxEL-G4Rkk3tpaNUE7569KSEt87kIW86DDxuMCsod-n9fP2-RyxSstWr8w72bTUxbPVF0ChNAB2x_keAadBZ)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESiAEBxCJF1_mOI6z9U48yGhYeul_NO92Kjzh128A6AMvH6-PtWNTufqSgUqySRcy4BN7lFB4pi1H_IICZu9W27a2bRX-B03bEeKXRoxJi5Dov0oA1pwvIpSjMYsacNuychBqVjPhtTcc8e-uQcgIyUAgghxcbyJJENhrT_-Oi2GygjnmOVLkPes6m)

### Factors That Influence It

- **Genetics:** Variations in ADH and ALDH genes change how quickly ethanol and acetaldehyde are processed, affecting alcohol tolerance, flushing, and health risks.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdgHEIkXXIp1BF5tL2rOTW2-LHHbffwhgkh3byH2zDWBF3YKJgFtIz_HVUBeXjwCx3fXbyyHN3ZJZUQdcV6MdGC2fUgJWLkMMjfJD_MbslHOd_GzkyFTZOp00EbAfZuvI7iN6EzmBBVuFBtYdj458TdmqyXUwIso)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbgHEIkXXFLcgtd6RR4ZbE5XIRbIIimYF656jc8sAsigCepxtoLbUtspVYkdgY3ttPUKthJn76FTfsfPZe_NLYIIBlO2qCgVdZOWpJZKpJDtznoC3wpJqPCCOjHcWDJAIHJ_R4E_9rWFxu-VVcVys)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESeQHEIkXXPyPmgZPwagj1Dd4OWuEMmagOaiWtk1ky76vYeyWfoJnlw3XAgGMnmqhAT6MYip4cP6W4VTYIVUYGQNx0CKb3EsAQvb33Gbhr3AAd4FjfcpDEGNmZTroxBOQncpGFphIIbhYH2p3PN8mcpx7XCWpbz37PvIY)
- **Food and Drinking Speed:** Eating food slows gastric emptying and affects absorption and elimination dynamics, while drinking quickly can overwhelm the liver's processing capacity.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESiAEBxCJF1_mOI6z9U48yGhYeul_NO92Kjzh128A6AMvH6-PtWNTufqSgUqySRcy4BN7lFB4pi1H_IICZu9W27a2bRX-B03bEeKXRoxJi5Dov0oA1pwvIpSjMYsacNuychBqVjPhtTcc8e-uQcgIyUAgghxcbyJJENhrT_-Oi2GygjnmOVLkPes6m)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbgHEIkXXFLcgtd6RR4ZbE5XIRbIIimYF656jc8sAsigCepxtoLbUtspVYkdgY3ttPUKthJn76FTfsfPZe_NLYIIBlO2qCgVdZOWpJZKpJDtznoC3wpJqPCCOjHcWDJAIHJ_R4E_9rWFxu-VVcVys)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEStgEBxCJF1586n34yf9ax6JJG1zHafunqJ5MVRPeB0tYrtKr6hQqOsEajxhO6D6E6xzkBKF7Cx3VTPbXy9HkN_TDVcIsB06Q1MAD3A6zwNsCSn5SSeuysplbhdjw5MbdIdK4OGEFs5iTR8w4kaW5Dsb0OGjvY2CvBh4fbEqcJem8Zmf1wYfw2otw_0QLUpZo_sSTOWnFFP1cG2KXOQ_sleiuL3gMccrApg2k7C-klh6LhlgyBCh5VtA)
- **Liver Health and Medications:** Liver damage or certain drugs (such as acetaminophen) can interfere with hepatic processing.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESnQEBxCJF16GZbKqjkpS5NWxe5Igs6f0Iu43bSWQXOGD732Vr3Vbcgn-9LjF0hlcb2V-hy7_T__ulsVDS64hFpm6a13obqzZGxdUARIRcyJ8KxwFfB_2FayF9736V4bs-fxEL-G4Rkk3tpaNUE7569KSEt87kIW86DDxuMCsod-n9fP2-RyxSstWr8w72bTUxbPVF0ChNAB2x_keAadBZ)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESlwEBxCJF11VA0JEqCBgXI7AJAn8mz2tqsJuBq81JHPiFsGeT5y55koG9gzZjcRaFcyA06flg8u43NUG7sFe_8MXRwhSofXiVFfXAaFbQ7thZPpgQMjIwbV4ecRFlv1gieMf2-yG8Fchnfdqpec_eu9R9Gj4rUeXZzwZ-LvbzgbMPgNQFlMpaiMKqBUFgQzjiwU5Cs_Ap6IcJ)

For a plain-language overview of how enzymes and acetaldehyde affect the body, see the [National Institute on Alcohol Abuse and Alcoholism](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdgHEIkXXIp1BF5tL2rOTW2-LHHbffwhgkh3byH2zDWBF3YKJgFtIz_HVUBeXjwCx3fXbyyHN3ZJZUQdcV6MdGC2fUgJWLkMMjfJD_MbslHOd_GzkyFTZOp00EbAfZuvI7iN6EzmBBVuFBtYdj458TdmqyXUwIso) . For deeper biochemical details on enzyme pathways and kinetics, see [PMC](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbgHEIkXXFLcgtd6RR4ZbE5XIRbIIimYF656jc8sAsigCepxtoLbUtspVYkdgY3ttPUKthJn76FTfsfPZe_NLYIIBlO2qCgVdZOWpJZKpJDtznoC3wpJqPCCOjHcWDJAIHJ_R4E_9rWFxu-VVcVys).[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdgHEIkXXIp1BF5tL2rOTW2-LHHbffwhgkh3byH2zDWBF3YKJgFtIz_HVUBeXjwCx3fXbyyHN3ZJZUQdcV6MdGC2fUgJWLkMMjfJD_MbslHOd_GzkyFTZOp00EbAfZuvI7iN6EzmBBVuFBtYdj458TdmqyXUwIso)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbgHEIkXXFLcgtd6RR4ZbE5XIRbIIimYF656jc8sAsigCepxtoLbUtspVYkdgY3ttPUKthJn76FTfsfPZe_NLYIIBlO2qCgVdZOWpJZKpJDtznoC3wpJqPCCOjHcWDJAIHJ_R4E_9rWFxu-VVcVys)Would you like to explore **genetic enzyme variations** (such as ALDH2 deficiency), **how alcohol interacts with medications and liver health** , or **factors that affect blood alcohol concentration**?

items.title: How the Body Breaks Down Alcohol
items.text: Absorption: After swallowing, alcohol enters the bloodstream mainly through the small intestine and stomach, then travels to the liver. Step 1 (Ethanol to Acetaldehyde): The enzyme alcohol dehydrogenase (ADH) converts ethanol into acetaldehyde, a toxic compound and known carcinogen. Step 2 (Acetaldehyde to Acetate): The enzyme aldehyde dehydrogenase (ALDH) —primarily mitochondrial ALDH2—quickly converts acetaldehyde into acetate, a less toxic substance. Final Elimination: Acetate moves out of the liver into other tissues, where it is broken down into carbon dioxide and water. Roughly 90%–98% of ingested ethanol is metabolized, while about 5%–10% is excreted unchanged via breath, urine, and sweat.

Drinking coffee, taking cold showers, or drinking water does not speed up this metabolic rate.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESlwEBxCJF11VA0JEqCBgXI7AJAn8mz2tqsJuBq81JHPiFsGeT5y55koG9gzZjcRaFcyA06flg8u43NUG7sFe_8MXRwhSofXiVFfXAaFbQ7thZPpgQMjIwbV4ecRFlv1gieMf2-yG8Fchnfdqpec_eu9R9Gj4rUeXZzwZ-LvbzgbMPgNQFlMpaiMKqBUFgQzjiwU5Cs_Ap6IcJ)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESnQEBxCJF16GZbKqjkpS5NWxe5Igs6f0Iu43bSWQXOGD732Vr3Vbcgn-9LjF0hlcb2V-hy7_T__ulsVDS64hFpm6a13obqzZGxdUARIRcyJ8KxwFfB_2FayF9736V4bs-fxEL-G4Rkk3tpaNUE7569KSEt87kIW86DDxuMCsod-n9fP2-RyxSstWr8w72bTUxbPVF0ChNAB2x_keAadBZ)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESiAEBxCJF1_mOI6z9U48yGhYeul_NO92Kjzh128A6AMvH6-PtWNTufqSgUqySRcy4BN7lFB4pi1H_IICZu9W27a2bRX-B03bEeKXRoxJi5Dov0oA1pwvIpSjMYsacNuychBqVjPhtTcc8e-uQcgIyUAgghxcbyJJENhrT_-Oi2GygjnmOVLkPes6m)

items.title: Factors That Influence It
items.text: Genetics: Variations in ADH and ALDH genes change how quickly ethanol and acetaldehyde are processed, affecting alcohol tolerance, flushing, and health risks. Food and Drinking Speed: Eating food slows gastric emptying and affects absorption and elimination dynamics, while drinking quickly can overwhelm the liver's processing capacity. Liver Health and Medications: Liver damage or certain drugs (such as acetaminophen) can interfere with hepatic processing.
items.markdown:
